title: Collect Coins in a Tree
summary: Given an undirected and unrooted tree with n nodes, where each node may contain a coin, you can collect coins from any node within a distance of 2 or move to any adjacent node.
statement: Given an undirected and unrooted tree with n nodes, where each node may contain a coin, you can collect coins from any node within a distance of 2 or move to any adjacent node. Determine the minimum number of edges you need to traverse to collect all the coins and return to the starting node, considering each edge traversal.
constraints: The inputs describe an undirected tree; coins[i] tells whether node i has a coin.
From a node you collect every coin within distance two, or you may traverse an adjacent edge.
Return the fewest edge traversals needed to collect every coin and finish where you started.
hints: First remove empty leaves: walking into them can never help collect a coin.
After that pruning, every remaining leaf has a coin.
Remove exactly two more leaf layers because their coins are collectable from two edges away.
Every surviving edge lies in the necessary core and must be traversed in both directions to return to the start.
editorial: Every surviving edge lies in the necessary core and must be traversed in both directions to return to the start.

tests.explanation: Starting at node two, walk once to node three and back; the two endpoint coins are within distance two.
After irrelevant leaves and two free collection layers are removed, two core edges must each be crossed twice.
